mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 650K units, indicating robust demand, boosts consumer confidence, leading to increased spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between HOUST and consumer confidence
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of instances when HOUST surpasses 650K, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% signals an accommodative monetary policy, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to decreased borrowing costs.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns when FEDFUNDS < 0.5% are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) drops below 8% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200K in a month, the combined signal of a strengthening labor market predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical labor market indicators and equity performance
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 30% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a quarter, signaling increased economic activity, leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies capitalize on growing demand.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns when INDPRO > 2% QoQ are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the GDP chained price index (GDPC1) by more than 1% in a quarter, indicating decreased inflationary pressures, predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as real incomes rise.
evidence_refs: fact:historical relationship between inflation and consumer spending
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 45% of instances when GDPC1 drops by more than 1%, or Rank IC < 0.015 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by less than 0.5% in a month, the combined signal of moderate inflation and high interest rates predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 40% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in two consecutive months, signaling labor market weakness, predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending decreases.
evidence_refs: fact:historical labor market indicators and consumer spending
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 35% of instances when UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% over 2 months, or Rank IC < 0.012 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Always-on signal: the level of real final sales (RSAFS) consistently predicts S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, with higher sales indicating positive returns due to increased economic activity.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.025 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns do not show a significant positive correlation with RSAFS levels (t-test p > 0.05).
